references.text: Warns against godlessness like that of Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal and afterward found no chance to repent
Esau complains that Jacob took his birthright – the consequence of the choice he made in Gen 25:32
'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die' – a similar short-sighted attitude as Esau's thinking that he would die anyway
Thematic connection to prioritizing immediate gratification over long-term blessing
The parable of the rich man and Lazarus – a warning against prioritizing the earthly over the eternal
Hebrews interprets Esau's action in Genesis as an example of godlessness and worldly prioritization.
